facts.statement: The genus Wodnika was described by Münster in 1843.
The genus Wodnika has the synonym Radamas.
The genus Wodnika includes three species: Wodnika althausi, Wodnika ocoyae, and Wodnika striatula.
facts.quote: subdivision: Wodnika althausi Wodnika ocoyae Wodnika striatula

facts.statement: Wodnika lived during the Late Permian period in what is now Germany and Russia.
facts.quote: Wodnika is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish which lived in the Late Permian period in the present area of Germany and Russia

facts.statement: Wodnika measured about 1 meter (3.2 feet) in length.
facts.quote: It measured about 1 m (3.2 ft) in length

facts.statement: The tail shape of Wodnika suggests it was likely a good swimmer.
facts.quote: its tail shape indicates it was probably a good swimmer

facts.statement: Fossils of Wodnika often preserve the internal cartilage skeleton, a rare feature for shark-like fish.
facts.quote: Internally, the cartilage skeleton is preserved on the fossil, which is fairly rare for fossilized shark-like chondrichthyans

facts.statement: Wodnika belongs to the parent group Ctenacanthoidea.
Wodnika is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Wodnika is listed as the Wordian to Burdigalian, spanning from 266.9 to 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Wordian to Burdigalian (266.9 to 15.98 million years ago)
